title: Aquatic Ecosystems
description: Dive deep into the ecosystems of our planet's waters.

questions.text: What percentage of Earth's water is salt water found in oceans and seas?
questions.explanationText: About 97% of Earth's water is saline, found in oceans. Only about 3% is freshwater, and most of that is locked in ice caps and glaciers.

questions.text: Which ocean zone receives the most sunlight, allowing photosynthesis to occur?
questions.explanationText: The photic or epipelagic zone is the top layer of the ocean (down to about 200 meters) where sunlight penetrates sufficiently for photosynthesis.

questions.text: What type of tiny, photosynthetic organisms form the base of most marine food webs?
questions.explanationText: Phytoplankton are microscopic marine algae that perform photosynthesis, producing oxygen and serving as the primary producers in the ocean.

questions.text: Coral reefs are built by colonies of tiny animals called polyps. Which organism lives symbiotically within them to provide food?
questions.explanationText: Zooxanthellae are photosynthetic algae that live inside coral tissues, providing corals with food and giving them their vibrant colors.

questions.text: What term describes a partially enclosed coastal body of water where freshwater from rivers mixes with salty ocean water?
questions.explanationText: An estuary is a highly productive transition zone where freshwater streams mix with saltwater from the ocean.

questions.text: What is the primary cause of ocean acidification?
questions.explanationText: Ocean acidification is primarily caused by the ocean absorbing excess carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere, forming carbonic acid.

questions.text: Which deep-sea ecosystem relies on geothermal energy and chemical synthesis rather than sunlight?
questions.explanationText: Hydrothermal vents support unique ecosystems through chemosynthesis, where bacteria convert mineral-rich chemical compounds from the Earth's crust into energy.
Marine snow is a continuous shower of organic material (detritus, dead plankton, fecal matter) falling from the upper waters to the deep ocean, feeding deep-sea organisms.

answers.text: Organic debris falling from upper water layers to the deep ocean

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest living structure on Earth, visible from space?
questions.explanationText: Located in Australia, the Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system and the largest living structure on Earth.

questions.text: What phenomenon occurs when corals expel their symbiotic algae due to stress, such as warming water temperatures?
questions.explanationText: Coral bleaching happens when stressed corals expel their zooxanthellae, turning white and leaving them vulnerable to disease and starvation.

questions.text: What term is used to describe the transition zone between two different ecosystems, such as where land meets sea?
questions.explanationText: An ecotone is a region of transition between two biological communities, containing species from both and often exhibiting high biodiversity.

questions.text: What is the main driver of global ocean currents, often called the 'Great Ocean Conveyor Belt'?
questions.explanationText: Thermohaline circulation is driven by global density gradients created by surface heat and freshwater fluxes (temperature and salinity).

questions.text: Which marine biome is characterized by trees with specialized root systems that can filter salt and thrive in coastal intertidal zones?
questions.explanationText: Mangroves are salt-tolerant trees that grow in coastal saline or brackish water, protecting coastlines from erosion and storm surges.
Eutrophication is caused by runoff (like agricultural fertilizers) containing nitrogen and phosphorus, causing rapid algae growth that depletes oxygen when it dies and decomposes.

answers.text: The process of water becoming more acidic
The accumulation of plastic waste in ocean gyres
Excessive nutrient enrichment in a body of water, leading to algal blooms and oxygen depletion
The natural evaporation of freshwater lakes

questions.text: What is the maximum depth of the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point in the Earth's oceans?
questions.explanationText: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is the deepest known point in Earth's oceans, reaching a depth of nearly 11,000 meters (approx. 36,000 feet).
